name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with two, three or four wheels, a saddle or seat, fully operative pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts and one brake horsepower, in one of three classes: Class I and Class II (throttle) stop at 20 mph, Class III (pedal assist) at 28 mph. Counted as a bicycle under the Nebraska Rules of the Road. Defined by Nebraska Revised Statutes §§60-611, 60-614.02 to 60-614.04 and 60-618.03, as enacted by LB 138 (2023), operative September 2, 2023.
restrictions: Class I assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; Class II can power it whether or not the rider pedals and stops at 20 mph; Class III assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
Two, three or four wheels, a saddle or seat, and fully operative pedals
Its motor may produce no more than 750 watts and no more than one brake horsepower
A bicycle under the Rules of the Road, with a bicycle's rights and duties
Not a motor vehicle or a motor-driven cycle: no driver's license, registration or insurance
No statewide minimum age for any class
No helmet requirement: the state helmet law covers motorcycles, autocycles and mopeds only
No speedometer or labeling requirement in state law
The state, its agencies and local governments may permit, restrict or ban it on areas they own or control, by regulation or posted signs; riding where it's banned is a Class III misdemeanor
A motorized bicycle outside these limits is a motor-driven cycle
